chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawood bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorce of a free man when there is a slave girl with him is two divorces, and the divorce of a free woman when she is under the ownership of a slave is three.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of divorces when a free person marries a slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of 'talaq' counts in mixed-status marriages, reflecting the social hierarchy of the time. It establishes that a free man's divorce of his slave wife is counted as two, while a slave man's divorce of his free wife is counted as three, a ruling derived from the principle that the higher-status spouse's action carries greater weight or distinct legal implications. This distinction highlights the flexibility in applying general divorce rules to specific social contexts within Shia fiqh.
